title: Pen Pal
credits: Words, music, arrangement, voice and picture by Claude. Sung by en_US-amy-medium through Praat PSOLA.
key: G major; the final chorus and outro lift a whole step to A major

lines.text: Save it. Clip it. Insert it. Export it.
Spin the hard disk. Feed the floppy.
Ask the question. Search it. Read it.
Clip the proof. Scrapbook. Keep it.
Outline it. Draft it. Your words. Not mine.
I can fetch. I can file.
I can hum for a while.
But the pen and the page
You say where the words land,
I sing it, you say it.
La la la, la la la la.
La la la, la la la la.
Chat is an app. Not the whole computer.
Too regular? Flag it. Generic? Flag it.
Press release? Flag it. Rough edge? Keep it.
I can check. I can flag.
I can point at the drift.
But the pen and the page
You say where the words land,
I sing it, you say it.
I sing it, you say it.
it still won't hold the pen.
You say where the words land,
I sing it, you say it.
I sing it, you say it.
Save it. Clip it. Insert it. Export it.

lead.why: en_US-amy-medium speaks near G3; sung notes stay within ~1.7 octaves above it so PSOLA keeps the words

chant.why: amy with the pitch tier flattened; D3 is the deadpan end-of-list fall

choir.why: written pitches; the production stacks amy + jenny + lessac (lessac an octave down is not notated)

spoken.why: unpitched raw TTS; the note slots are time only

machineVoice.chant: amy, pitch tier flattened to the written note (G3 = her speaking pitch), no vibrato; durations quantised to the 8th grid; only the vowel nucleus is stretched (duration tier holds onsets/codas at 1.0); doubled an octave down by lessac at -9 dB; 1988 sections add an 8-bit 11 kHz crush; the last word of every list line steps down to D3
machineVoice.lead: amy singing; gentle vibrato (5.5 Hz, +/-20 cents) on notes of 1 beat or longer; 60 ms portamento only where notes are slurred inside a word
machineVoice.choir: amy + en_GB-jenny_dioco + lessac (an octave down), each offset +/-15 ms and detuned +/-8 cents; the final chorus doubles every voice (6 takes) and adds a 12-copy gang on the echoes, one copy per appearance
machineVoice.spoken: lessac, raw Piper, no PSOLA; k1 is low-passed to 4 kHz with an 8-bit crush (a sample from a 1988 Mac); o3 is dry and flat, the full-disk-warning voice

melt.pre1a / pre2a: flat chant on G3, octave double, crush
melt.pre1b / pre2b: chant with an 80 ms glide between notes (the robot learns portamento); crush lifts
melt.pre1c / pre2c: lead: vibrato arrives, octave double removed
melt.pre1d / pre2d: full lead, ending on D5 HAND; everything else stops

gags.fade (chorus d lines): level fade and pitch glide B4 -> G4 while the bit depth drops over the 1.5 beats: the word is literally temporary
gags.erase (chorus h lines): a reverse-reverb swell before 'erase'; the 'it' is bone dry
gags.chorus3b 'pen' (silent=true): the lead does not sing the word; one beat of silence and a single keystroke; the band slams back on 'You say'
gags.v2c 'Too regular? Flag it.': the chant is perfectly regular on purpose, so Review Desk flags the singer; the band answers with the one-beat stumble (fills.stumble)
gags.chorus3g 'Your roughness is you': +/-10 cent detune and 20 ms unquantised onsets on the lead: the machine tries roughness for one line
gags.bridge years: chant stacked in octaves, panned; a system beep on every year (parts.beeps)
gags.o2 'voice': the long A4 freezes into a two-cycle grain loop for its last half beat, then the boot chord takes over

machineVoice.qa: faster_whisper small.en must transcribe every line word for word; if a line fails, lengthen its slowest word or move its echo

bootChord.timbre: saw pad + FM bell, sharp attack, low-pass opening slowly over 4 beats, then ringing; ours, not Apple's

rebootChord.timbre: the boot chord voiced in A, with a crash: the reboot into Liquid Glass

outroChord.timbre: the boot chord in A, ringing to the end; the 9th never resolves

riff.name: The Floppy Organ
riff.timbre: percussive combo organ (FluidR3 GM 17) doubled by a numpy 25%-duty pulse; each attack gets a 6 ms downward pitch blip and a very quiet floppy-stepper click (band-passed noise 2-3 kHz, 8 ms); 8-bit 11 kHz sample-and-hold crush in 1988 sections, lifting as the eras advance, fully clean in Liquid Glass

plays.note: under the call and response; the choir then sings it on la (organ tacet)
full loop, second organ an octave down
in A Mixolydian, clean, with the last chant

riff.headFillsNote: the 3-note head (G B D) as a pickup fill into chorus bars 5 and into the next section; glockenspiel (GM 10) doubles it an octave up in the final chorus

glockDouble.what: glockenspiel doubles the head fills and plays the loop on top of the outro

styles.pulse8: big-beat bass: two detuned saws, root 8ths, sidechain pump from the kick
styles.octaveBounce: round finger bass (GM 34) alternating root / octave on 8ths, after Feel It Still
styles.long: sustained roots (pre-chorus: under the string pad; breakdown: a soft sine sub)

cuts: bar 1 of the breakdown: only the G pedal and the spoken sample
the D pivot bar: riser only, the pickup is a cappella
voice and piano, then the boot chord

drums.gridNote: 16 characters per bar, one per 16th; a pattern of 1/2/4 bars repeats through its section

kit.kick: 55 Hz sine + click (big-beat) / tighter 808 in the choruses
kit.clap: layered noise bursts, three copies 8 ms apart

mutes: stop-time on HAND: only a reverse cymbal
the silent pen: one keystroke, nothing else

fills.name: riser1
fills.what: white-noise riser under the string pad

fills.name: stumble
fills.what: on 'Too regular? Flag it.' the fill lands a 16th late: the band loosening up after the flag

fills.name: bridgeRoll
fills.what: snare roll + filter sweep into the breakdown

fills.name: spinUp
fills.what: floppy-drive spin-up riser (sine sweep + comb grit) on the D pivot

fills.name: reboot
fills.what: white flash: crash + the boot chord in A

fills.name: keystroke
fills.what: one dry keyboard click: the writer types 'pen'

fills.name: slamBack
fills.what: crash: the band returns on 'You say'

fills.name: crash3
fills.what: crash on the second pen pal

sections.intro: organ riff only, no pads; dry
sections.verse1: organ riff; a filtered UI blip (sine ping, 30 ms) on every chant verb (use the chant word starts)
sections.pre1: string pad (GM 49) sustaining each chord voicing, rising with the riser; the riff drops out
sections.chorus1: bouncy offbeat piano 8ths (GM 1) on the chord voicings; soft saw pad; brass stabs (GM 62) listed in stabs.brass; glockenspiel ping on every 'pen' (stabs.glockPen); one tenor sax (GM 66) stab after 'erase it'
sections.post1: organ riff bars 1-2; bars 3-4 the choir sings the riff over a vinyl-crackle bed (One More Tune's record)
sections.verse2: as verse 1 plus a second organ an octave down
sections.chorus2: as chorus 1, bass doubled, tambourine 16ths, choir harmony a third below on bars 5-8
sections.post2: organ riff, cowbell and claps on every beat
sections.bridge: the loop follows the bridge chords; a system beep per year (parts.beeps) climbing like an arpeggio; bars 7-8 a filter-swept pad, half-time drums building
sections.breakdown: bar 1: a G pedal (sine) and the spoken sample only; bars 2-4: felt piano (GM 1, soft) on the voicings, snaps and claps, lots of space; bar 4 the floppy spin-up riser on D, the pickup a cappella
sections.chorus3: the reboot chord with a crash, then everything in A: piano, pad, brass, glock doubling the riff head, 12-copy gang on the echoes; bar 2 beat 4 is one beat of silence (the keystroke); sax stab on FADE and after 'erase it'
sections.outro: bars 1-2 riff and loop in A under the chant; bar 3 piano and claps under the lead alone; bar 4 the Amaj9 boot chord rings and the spoken line sits over it
sections.tail: the boot chord decaying; one mouse click at saveClick; silence for the end card

keys.voicings: take each chord's 'notes' from the chords list: bass note first, then a close voicing around C4

counterChant.what: optional: 'Save it. Clip it. Insert it. Export it.' chanted on A3 at -12 dB under final-chorus bars 3-4 and 7-8; not a captioned line

sfx.uiBlips: one 30 ms sine ping on every chant word that starts on an integer beat (verses, intro)
